title: Tokyo's Sushi Bus Combines Food and Sightseeing
paragraphs: In Tokyo, tourists can now eat sushi and see the city at the same time. A new tour bus has a conveyor belt for sushi.

The SUSHI BUS started its tours on October 10, 2026. It is a 12-meter-long bus with two floors, and the top floor has no roof. A picture of tuna sushi covers the outside of the bus. Around the seats on the top floor, there is a conveyor belt that carries plates of sushi. The sushi is made in a small kitchen on the lower floor, and a lift brings it up to the top.

The tour starts near Tokyo Station and takes 70 minutes. The bus passes famous places, such as Tokyo Tower, Tokyo Skytree and Kaminarimon Gate in Asakusa. Guests can eat as much sushi as they want. There are about 12 kinds of sushi, such as tuna, salmon, shrimp and octopus. The fish comes from Toyosu Market. The tour costs 16,000 yen.

How does the sushi stay on the belt when the bus moves? The company spent two and a half years making the bus. It tested the plates more than 100 times to check that they do not fall when the bus stops suddenly. The bus only goes up to about 30 kilometers per hour, so the soy sauce does not spill. When it rains, a clear roof covers the top floor.

There are five tours a day, and each tour has 20 seats. About seven in 10 customers are Japanese, but the company mainly wants to attract foreign tourists. In the future, it hopes to start tours in other cities.
